insight.title: Why Learning From Success Can Mislead You
insight.subtitle: How focusing only on winners distorts your strategy

sections.text: We naturally study successful companies to replicate their path. This common practice, however, often overlooks a critical factor: the vast graveyard of similar failures. It's called survival bias.

Survival bias makes us only see what endures, like judging market entry by existing giants without seeing the thousands who tried and vanished. It skews our understanding of true probabilities and risks.

In business, this means overestimating success rates and misinterpreting causes. You might emulate a winning strategy, unaware it's merely one lucky outcome among countless identical attempts that failed silently.
Try this today: The next time you analyze a business success today, mentally list three similar failures you *don't* see.
The loudest lessons come from the few who made it; the truer lessons are often buried with the many who didn't.
